ev.q: This report presents national, state-level, and county-level point estimates and 95% CIs for the prevalence of depression.
The age-standardized prevalence of depression among U.S. adults was 18.5%
pairwise t-tests were used to determine differences (compared with a reference category) by age group, sex, race or ethnicity, and education level
The multilevel logistic regression model included depression as the binary dependent variable.
All prevalence estimates were age standardized to the 2000 U.S. Census Bureau population.
CDC analyzed 2020 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) data to estimate the national, state-level, and county-level prevalence
BRFSS is an ongoing, state-based, random-digit–dialed landline and cell phone survey
Among 3,143 counties, the model-based age-standardized prevalence of depression ranged from 10.7% to 31.9%
